title: Benefit Offset Terms Table, Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery
content:
How much of a VA benefit payment is withheld for a debt, and from which benefit lines, for each debt type in **Benefit Debts and Overpayment Recovery**.

| Debt type | Share of each benefit payment withheld with no plan in effect (percent) | Benefit lines offset | Retroactive release offset up to the full balance under reduced withholding | After the debtor's death, collection only against the estate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Education Overpayment (Chapters 30, 35 and 1606) | 100 | Compensation, pension, education | Yes | Yes |
| Post-9/11 GI Bill Housing and Books Overpayment | 100 | Compensation, pension, education | Yes | Yes |
| Post-9/11 GI Bill Tuition and Fees Overpayment | 100 | Compensation, pension, education | Yes | Yes |
| Disability Compensation Overpayment | 100 | Compensation, pension, education | Yes | Yes |
| Veterans Pension Overpayment | 100 | Compensation, pension, education | Yes | Yes |
| Home Loan Guaranty Debt | 100 | Compensation, pension, education | Yes | Yes |

## Column meanings

- **Share withheld** — the share of each benefit payment withheld while a debt is in active collection and no plan applies. At 100 percent, the whole payment is withheld, never more than the remaining balance.
- **Benefit lines offset** — the benefit lines from which this debt type can be collected by offset: Disability Compensation, Veterans Pension and education payments for every debt type.
- **Retroactive release** — whether a retroactive benefit release is offset up to the full outstanding balance even while a reduced-withholding plan is in effect. It is Yes for every type.
- **Estate only** — whether, after the debtor's death, collection proceeds only against the estate and benefit offsets stop. It is Yes for every type.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A monthly pension payment of 900.00 USD against a debt with 400.00 USD remaining is withheld 400.00 USD, the remaining balance, and not the full 900.00 USD.
